doc.title: Flip Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 11, 1996

title: Radio, television and why TV hurt jazz
summary: Radio was everything then; he argues television favored performers who moved and used lights.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Radio was the only thing then. There was no television you know. Every town you went to they played them, you’d make interviews, and it was, radio was the whole thing. Not like today. Television knocked us out of the box.
Yeah. Other people have said that.

My opinion. ‘Cause we didn’t move around as much as these people, jumping up in the air, coming out of the earth, coming out of the grave and jumping with the lights. We didn’t do that. Oscar Peterson played a hell of a piano you know, but he didn’t jump down in the thing, he didn’t have the lights flashing. Jacquet could move, I could move, but we didn’t have the lights. And these guys came along with the lights and jumping
from the ceilings and all of that, and that what, television is moving pictures, and that’s what the people want to see you move. It’s moving pictures.
